title: TwinStream infosec technical appendix and workshop notes
content:
Executive summary:

This document is the technical appendix and workshop readout for the TwinStream Health POC (Feb 2026). It bundles the infosec questionnaire responses we committed to during the onsite workshop, an indexed list of submitted evidence artifacts, a short risk/open-item register for compliance reviewers, and minutes/action items from the security working session on 2026-02-18. The intention is to provide a single-file snapshot that auditors or TwinStream security reviewers can use to validate our environment and controls for the proposed Dedicated deployment.

POC scope recap:
- Customer: TwinStream Health (clinical data integrations, non-PHI proof-of-concept only during initial phase).
- Deployment mode evaluated: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in us-west-2) with optional VPC peering for private connectivity.
- Workloads: low-latency chat generation and embeddings for triage routing.
- Data classification: POC limited to de-identified clinical text (customer asserted). No PHI stored in Redwood-hosted artifacts per POC agreement.

Submitted evidence index (artifact name -> short description):
1) rs-infra-arch-v1.png -> logical diagram showing dedicated pool, VPC peering, NAT/firewall boundaries, and private control plane connectivity.
2) rs-kms-policy-snapshot.txt -> minimal KMS policy used for POC key with ARNs redacted for public copy.
3) rs-audit-sample-logs-20260214.csv -> sample access logs (token-level redaction applied); shows admin actions and model deployment timestamps.
4) rs-deploy-runbook-twinstream.md -> step-by-step deploy runbook used by solutions engineering during POC.
5) rs-priv-net-config.txt -> sanitized VPC peering CIDR blocks and routing table summary.
6) rs-quantization-profile-emb-2.json -> model runtime profile used (performance/cost tradeoff summary).
7) rs-penetration-notes-quickscan.pdf -> short internal pentest notes from red-team quick scan during POC (findings: outstanding non-prod S3 ACL; remediated).
8) rs-contract-nda-signed.pdf -> redacted NDA signed by TwinStream POC lead.

Questionnaire highlights and curated responses (selected):
- Q: How are customer requests authenticated to the Dedicated endpoint?
  A: Mutual TLS between customer gateway and Redwood edge + token-based service auth for control plane. For the POC we used temporary mTLS certs issued by Redwood CA; control-plane operations required a short-lived API token. See artifact rs-kms-policy-snapshot.txt and rs-infra-arch-v1.png.

- Q: Where is customer data persisted and how is it segregated?
  A: During the POC all request/response payloads were held in volatile in-memory KV cache on the inference nodes and were not written to long-term storage. Model artifacts are in a customer-scoped model registry with ACLs; telemetry and aggregated metrics are written to a dedicated metrics namespace accessible only to Redwood SRE and the customer. Evidence: rs-deploy-runbook-twinstream.md and rs-audit-sample-logs-20260214.csv.

- Q: What KMS/HSM protections are in use?
  A: Root keys in AWS KMS with automatic rotation enabled. For Dedicated customers we support BYOK and HSM integrations; the POC used a Redwood-managed key with a narrowly scoped policy. See rs-kms-policy-snapshot.txt.

Architecture and control notes:
- Logical segregation: Dedicated GPU pool runs in a dedicated EC2 / ASG construct with IAM roles scoped to the pool. Control-plane calls (model rollouts, configuration changes) traverse a private control channel separate from inference data path.
- Network: VPC peering used for private data ingress; NAT gateways used for limited egress (updates/telemetry). Security group rules are principle-of-least-privilege.
- Runtime: inference nodes run with non-root containers; KV caches are ephemeral and cleared on pod termination. Quantization profiles are applied at model load time; no customer keys are embedded in image layers.

Risk register (open items and mitigations):
- Item 1: Verification of de-identification for dataset provided by TwinStream. Owner: TwinStream security. Mitigation: TwinStream to provide a sampling and validation check (due 2026-02-24).
- Item 2: Long-term log access scope — TwinStream requested 90-day audit logs with agent-level detail. Owner: Avery Chen; Action: provide export job template and storage lifecycle recommendation (ETA 2026-02-22).
- Item 3: HSM integration proof for production Dedicated (customer requested FIPS-140-2 evidence). Owner: Priya Patel; Action: gather vendor HSM attestation docs and map to Redwood's KMS integration flow (ETA 2026-03-05).

Workshop minutes (2026-02-18 security session) - key decisions:
- Decided to restrict POC to de-identified data only; TwinStream will sign an attestation (NDA addendum) that POC datasets are PHI-free.
- Agreed to provide a curated log sample rather than full access for initial security review.
- TwinStream requested an architecture walkthrough focused on key rotation, key escrow, and emergency key revocation — action item assigned to Priya.

Operational reproducibility checklist (what we handed them during the workshop):
- Repro steps for deploying a dedicated pool (rs-deploy-runbook-twinstream.md).
- How to request temporary mTLS certs for the POC (step-by-step).
- Log export template and redaction guidance (sample included in rs-audit-sample-logs-20260214.csv).

Known remediation history (short):
- 2026-02-14: internal quickscan flagged permissive non-prod S3 ACL; fixed by solutions engineering, revalidated 2026-02-16. Evidence: rs-penetration-notes-quickscan.pdf.

Next steps and owner assignments:
- TwinStream to deliver representative sample of de-identified messages (owner: TwinStream Security) by 2026-02-24.
- Avery Chen to deliver log export template + lifecycle recommendation by 2026-02-22.
- Priya Patel to compile HSM attestation pack and mapping by 2026-03-05.
- Marcus Rivera to run a second smoke test of VPC peering and provide connectivity verification (evidence artifact rs-vpc-peering-verify-20260219.txt) by 2026-02-19 (already submitted).

Appendix: quick artifact access notes for reviewers:
- All artifacts with PII/PHI redactions are marked with a leading rs- and were uploaded to the shared S3 bucket under s3://redwood-poc-evidence/twinstream/ (access controlled; contact solutions-eng for one-time presigned links).
- Confluence page SEC-arc-twinstream-2026 contains the canonical architecture and versioned diagrams.

If reviewers want an exec-level short packet for procurement or legal (one page), we can produce a condensed "Assurance Brief" summarizing controls and SLA commitments — requester: TwinStream legal or procurement.

Document owner/contact: Avery Chen (solutions-engineering) — achen@redwood.ai

Notes to internal reviewers: tag this doc with the customer code when you upload any new artifacts. Keep last_modified updated when artifacts change.
